items.title: Ada Lovelace
items.description: Wrote the first published algorithm intended for a machine, and imagined how computers could create more than numbers.

items.title: Charles Babbage
items.description: Designed the Analytical Engine, a programmable mechanical computer that inspired generations of computing ideas.

items.title: Alan Turing
items.description: Defined the theoretical model of computation and helped break the Enigma cipher during World War II.

items.title: Grace Hopper
items.description: Pioneered compilers and helped shape COBOL, making programming more accessible and portable.

items.title: John von Neumann
items.description: Formulated the stored-program architecture that underlies most modern computers.

items.title: Claude Shannon
items.description: Founded information theory and showed how digital circuits could implement logic.

items.title: Edsger Dijkstra
items.description: Advanced structured programming and created foundational graph algorithms.

items.title: Donald Knuth
items.description: Authored The Art of Computer Programming and shaped algorithm analysis and typographic computing.

items.title: Barbara Liskov
items.description: Led work on data abstraction, the Liskov Substitution Principle, and programming language design.

items.title: Tim Berners-Lee
items.description: Invented the World Wide Web, including HTTP, HTML, and the first web browser.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton
items.description: Directed Apollo flight software engineering and popularized the term 'software engineering'.

items.title: Dennis Ritchie
items.description: Created the C programming language and co-developed the UNIX operating system.

items.title: Ken Thompson
items.description: Co-created UNIX and wrote the B language, a direct ancestor of C.

items.title: John McCarthy
items.description: Coined the term 'artificial intelligence' and created the Lisp programming language.

items.title: Marvin Minsky
items.description: Co-founded the MIT AI Lab and contributed to early AI theory and robotics.

items.title: George Boole
items.description: Developed Boolean algebra, the mathematical foundation of digital logic.

items.title: Alonzo Church
items.description: Helped define computability with the lambda calculus and the Church-Turing thesis.

items.title: Niklaus Wirth
items.description: Designed Pascal and Modula, advancing language design and structured programming.

items.title: Seymour Cray
items.description: Architected groundbreaking supercomputers and pushed high-performance computing forward.

items.title: Frances Allen
items.description: Pioneered compiler optimization and parallel computing; first woman to win the Turing Award.
